Subject: Lockbox-proxy: VPC/on-prem key lifecycle & design kickoff

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for taking this on. We want to run a formal design review for the Lockbox Systems 'lockbox-proxy' deployment. High level: Lockbox will deploy a small on-prem appliance that stores customer KEKs in a vendor HSM (nShield/AzureHSM — TBD) and proxies wrapping keys back to the application layer in our VPC. We need Redwood's guidance on secure network topology, BYOK handoff, operator ceremony/rotation, and telemetry/audit expectations for SOC2 evidence.

Attached: lockbox_kms_network_diagram.pdf (diagram v1), requirements_matrix.xlsx (security + ops requirements), deployment_checklist.md (initial ask).

Immediate asks:
- Can Redwood support an HSM-attested gateway that performs wrap/unwrap without storing plaintext keys?
- Recommended rotation cadence and the ability to do emergency zeroize remotely vs on-site?
- Minimum network path: direct cross-connect vs IPsec VPN?
- Audit log retention and proof-of-possession evidence Redwood can provide for our auditors.

We'd like a 60-minute architecture sync early next week (PST). Proposed time windows: Mon/Tue morning.

Thanks,
Evan Ross
Head of Platform Security
Lockbox Systems

Evan — thanks for the clear packet. We can definitely support the high-level flows you described; a few clarifying notes before the sync so we come prepared:

Summary of what we'll cover at the sync (60m):
- Network topologies we recommend (private cross-connect, direct peering, and IPsec fallback) and tradeoffs for egress controls.
- HSM/BYOK patterns: attested gateway, wrapped KEK models, and split custody options.
- Rotation & ceremonies: online vs offline, operator roles, audit evidence, and rollback plans.
- Observability & evidence: token-level tracing, per-key audit trails, and exportable artifacts for SOC2.

Questions for you before the call (short answers ok):
1) Primary HSM vendor preference (so we can surface recommended attestation flows): nShield, Thales, AzureHSM, or vendor-neutral PKCS#11?
2) Do you require the HSM to be in your rack (on-prem) or a colocated provider (customer-controlled)?
3) Rotation SLA: what's acceptable downtime (if any) and max RPO for wrapped key availability?
4) Operator model: do you want Lockbox-only operators, Redwood observer-only, or split-keeper model?

Technical note: our Redwood Private control plane supports an HSM-attested gateway that never exports unwrapped KEKs. We typically recommend an ephemeral KEK per session (KEK derived from HSM master and ephemeral nonce) so application-level plaintext keys are never at rest on the proxy. We'll bring a short checklist for the sync: 'minimal required firewall rules', 'mutual-TLS fingerprinting', 'expected ports', and 'documented roll-forward/rollback steps'.

Propose: Mon 21 Dec 09:30 PST. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and a pre-read with a short network sketch we prefer.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Evan / team — quick notes ahead of Monday's call. I pulled together our recommended pattern for a lockbox-proxy that minimizes exposure while keeping your operator model operational. Main items:

1) Key model (recommended):
- Root HSM Master: stored in a FIPS-validated HSM in customer-controlled rack/colocation.
- KEK wrapping: application DEKs are wrapped by a per-tenant KEK derived inside the HSM (no plaintext export).
- Ephemeral session keys: for traffic-level operations we recommend short-lived session KEKs rotated per hour (or per connection if low-volume).

2) Custody & access:
- Split-custody for critical unseal keys: require two operators for any manual unseal or rotation ceremony.
- Redwood observer role: operator logs + read-only witness credentials (for audit) — Redwood should not have recovery-only capability unless explicitly configured (contractual SLA/escrow).

3) Rotation & rehearsals:
- Nominal rotation cadence: monthly wrap-KEK rotation, quarterly HSM master review (depends on compliance).
- Emergency zeroize: must be manual on-site (preferred) but we can provide signed remote zeroize triggers when physical access is impossible; remote triggers require multi-party attestations and will be recorded in audit trail.

4) Network & connectivity:
- Primary: private cross-connect (L2 or L3) between customer on-prem and Redwood VPC with access list to lockbox-proxy IPs only.
- Fallback: IPsec site-to-site with mutual TLS and certificate pinning on both ends.
- Ports: allow 443 (mutual TLS), 8443 (management plane), SSH (bastion limited / jump host), NTP to restricted stratum servers.

5) Audit & evidence:
- Per-key append-only logs, HSM module-generated proof-of-possession signed artifacts (PKCS#7), and daily digest uploads to a tamper-evident S3 bucket in your account.

6) Operational runbooks:
- Include a 'rotation playbook' with exact API calls, operator CLI commands, and expected date/time windows. We'll provide a template runbook in the pre-read.

Open questions for Lockbox:
- Does procurement allow a hardware HSM (nShield/Thales) vs managed HSM in customer-controlled cloud?
- Any constraints on telemetry export (some regulated customers require all telemetry to be kept on-prem).

I'll prepare a one-page 'Design Acceptance Checklist' and drop it in the meeting invite. Looking forward to the sync.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Principal Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Aditya — solid notes, thanks. Quick answers before the call on Wed:

- HSM vendor: our procurement prefers Thales nShield (we have two units in our rack already).
- HSM location: will be in our physical rack in a colo we control.
- Rotation SLAs: monthly rotation cadence is acceptable; emergency zeroize must be possible remotely for our off-site DR site but for the primary deployment we'd prefer on-site zeroize only.
- Operator model: split-custody with Lockbox operators performing hands-on tasks; Redwood as witness/observer is fine but Redwood cannot hold recovery keys (contractual constraint).
- Telemetry: we require that high-granularity telemetry for key usage remains in our account. Aggregated telemetry and token latency metrics can be shared to Redwood.

We'll confirm Wed 21 Dec 10:00 PST (sorry for the confusion — our team is on PST, not EST). Please send the invite to Evan, Priya, and lockbox-devops. We'll have our infra lead on the call and can provide SSH/console screenshots of the HSM.

Looking forward to the run-through.

Best,
Evan Ross
Head of Platform Security, Lockbox Systems
